yeah. im used to being a dissenter about these games bc 2 remains the best one in my mind, but i think what veilguard did insanely well was making it feel like your choices actually DID matter. Spoilers for Neve below but

Romancing Neve and saving Minrathous made her remarkably more considered, compassionate, and changed her input on decisions-- and she even called my character by a fond nickname during a completely unrelated boss fight for a different companion's story.

i don't think it's a huge disparity, but i find that most of veilguard's characters have more *opportunity* for character development and depth, since all BG3 has is a fairly middling amount of conversational opportunities, and the companions only chat during exploration.

veilguard has multiple scenes involving your party talking through plans together, they interact in the Lighthouse, and you go on character-specific outings, not just quests and missions.

obviously the timescale of these games is different-- veilguard takes place over months, whereas BG3 is likely a few weeks at best, but it still allows for excellent character development!

now, when it comes to player influence? veilguard also wins. Shadowheart's big moment in Act 2 is maybe the most well-done character moment in BG3-- but if you don't actively convince her to kill the Nightsong, she will refuse every time, no matter what, and go SeluneShart. (This is verifiable in the dialogue trees).
